Definition: from G1722 and G1416 (in the sense of sinking into a garment); to invest with clothing (literally or figuratively):--array, clothe (with), endue, have (put) on.
BiblicalUsage: To put on, as a garment. This corruptible must put on incorruption in 1 Corinthians 15:53, we put on the breastplate of faith and love in 1 Thessalonians 5:8, and Paul hopes that being clothed we shall not be found naked in 2 Corinthians 5:3. The word also dresses a king: Herod arrayed in royal apparel sat on his throne in Acts 12:21.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe putting on Christ is the daily work of the Christian — I put on the breastplate in the morning and I will put on incorruption at the last trumpet. I hold that what I wear spiritually matters more than what I wear outwardly, because God sees the clothing of the heart.
RelatedTopics: Identity in Christ; Resurrection; Spiritual Warfare
